preconditions.expression: all(3 <= int(x) <= 10**5 for x in [n, m]) and 0 <= m <= 10**5 and 1 <= v <= n
preconditions.description: Input consists of integers n (number of servers), m (number of connections), and v (failing server index), where n is between 3 and 10^5, m is between 0 and 10^5, and v is between 1 and n.
The first line of input contains exactly three space-separated integers: n, m, and v.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or (all(len(line.split()) == 2 for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()) and len(stdout.strip().splitlines()) == m)
postconditions.description: If no valid configuration exists, output is exactly '-1'. Otherwise, output consists of exactly m lines, each containing two distinct integers representing a valid connection between servers.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or (all(1 <= int(u) <= n and 1 <= int(w) <= n and u != w for line in stdout.strip().splitlines() for u, w in [line.split()]) and all(u < w or (u == w and False) for line in stdout.strip().splitlines() for u, w in [line.split()]))
postconditions.description: Each connection in the output is between two distinct servers (1 ≤ u, w ≤ n, u ≠ w), and each connection is listed exactly once (no duplicates).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' and (all(1 <= int(u) <= n and 1 <= int(w) <= n and u != w for line in stdout.strip().splitlines() for u, w in [line.split()]) and len(set((min(int(u), int(w)), max(int(u), int(w))) for line in stdout.strip().splitlines() for u, w in [line.split()])) == m)
postconditions.description: The output connections form a simple undirected graph with exactly m edges (no self-loops or duplicate edges).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' and (all(1 <= int(u) <= n and 1 <= int(w) <= n and u != w for line in stdout.strip().splitlines() for u, w in [line.split()]) and any(all(int(u) != v and int(w) != v for u, w in [line.split()]) for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()))
postconditions.description: The output graph is connected (there exists a path between any two servers) when all servers are operational.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' and (all(1 <= int(u) <= n and 1 <= int(w) <= n and u != w for line in stdout.strip().splitlines() for u, w in [line.split()]) and not any(all(int(u) != v and int(w) != v for u, w in [line.split()]) for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()) and not (all(int(u) != v or int(w) != v for u, w in [line.split()]) and any(int(u) == v or int(w) == v for u, w in [line.split()])))
postconditions.description: The output graph becomes disconnected when server v fails (i.e., removing server v and all its incident edges disconnects the graph).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' and (all(1 <= int(u) <= n and 1 <= int(w) <= n and u != w for line in stdout.strip().splitlines() for u, w in [line.split()]) and m >= n - 1 and m <= n * (n - 1) // 2)
postconditions.description: The number of connections m is feasible (n-1 ≤ m ≤ n(n-1)/2), where n-1 is the minimum for connectivity and n(n-1)/2 is the maximum possible edges in a simple graph.
